source_review.notes: Checked current Spark SQL performance, Web UI, configuration, and monitoring documentation; current Flink adaptive-batch scheduler, API, and recovery documentation; current Trino adaptive-plan, fault-tolerant-execution, and EXPLAIN cost documentation; and foundational Adaptive Query Processing, mid-query reoptimization, and Spark SQL primary sources. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Two alternate archival paper URLs returning HTTP 403 were excluded. Product capabilities and limitations are attributed rather than generalized.

evidence: Reviewed old/new continuation, remaining cost, decision, transition, discard, margin, query/snapshot/parameter, observation, materialization, and committed-output notation.
Reviewed bounded parallelism, partition bytes/times/attempts, median-relative skew, estimate log error, and revision epochs.
Checked positivity, nonnegative costs, dimensionally compatible comparisons, integer rounding, bounds, and uncertainty qualifications.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Estimated, observed, complete, remaining, sunk, reusable, discarded, and committed quantities remain distinct.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced net_savings=240, switch=yes, partitions=400, skew_threshold_mib=7680, and is_skewed=yes.
Recomputed 800 GiB divided by a 2 GiB target as 400 tasks within bounds 64–512.
Recomputed Exercise 2 as 3.2 TiB = 3276.8 GiB and ceil(3276.8/4) = 820 tasks within bounds 128–1,024.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Arithmetic demonstrates policy calculations; it does not prove semantic legality, memory feasibility, or production speedup.

evidence: Verified net remaining saving subtracts candidate, decision, transition, and discarded-work cost from the old remaining continuation before comparison with margin.
Verified p=min(p_max,max(p_min,ceil(B/T))) enforces integer downstream parallelism within declared bounds for positive target T.
Verified the absolute log error is symmetric for reciprocal multiplicative errors in the zero-free case and the skew gate combines median-relative and absolute floors.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Estimate error is diagnostic; candidate validity, feasibility, and remaining benefit are separate gates.

evidence: Reviewed zero/partial/complete observations, empty and huge intermediates, compressed-to-decoded expansion, tiny partitions, hot keys, and noisy thresholds.
Reviewed null/outer/semi/anti joins, nondeterministic or erroring expressions, ordering, collations, snapshots, connectors, and already emitted output.
Reviewed retries, speculation, cancellation races, stale epochs, optimizer timeout/crash, coordinator recovery, missing/corrupt shuffle, memory pressure, worker loss, and commit failure.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Incomplete, incompatible, infeasible, over-budget, or failed adaptation retains or reconstructs a conservative valid plan.

evidence: Traced fixed logical plan, parameters, snapshot, authorization, functions, row semantics, and output contract across immutable physical plan epochs.
Checked schema, encoding, partition map, hash/range function, ordering, snapshot, checksum, and producing epoch before intermediate reuse.
Checked one selected attempt per logical partition, authorized epoch-aware output commit, cancellation fencing, revision logging, and fallback.
invariant_checking.notes: Relational equivalence, state compatibility, physical properties, resource feasibility, and execution fencing are distinct obligations.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step revision argument from fixed semantics and validated observations through candidate legality, feasibility, cost, atomic installation, and verification.
Checked why partial bytes can monotonically disqualify an exceeded broadcast cap but cannot prove the completed relation fits.
Checked output-commit reasoning prevents old/new epoch duplicates and why non-retractable output constrains revision scope.
proof_review.notes: Economic eligibility cannot substitute for semantic, state, property, recovery, or commit correctness.

evidence: Audited adaptive query execution, observation point, decision point, materialization boundary, plan revision, state compatibility, transition cost, hysteresis, fallback, and budget terminology.

Confirmed static robust plans, precomputed alternatives, stage-boundary reoptimization, continuous routing, rule-based choice, cost-based choice, reuse, migration, and recomputation are differentiated.
Confirmed coalescing, skew splitting, broadcast conversion, shuffled-hash conversion, input reordering, local reading, and resource adaptation are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Each adaptation identifies its evidence, safe boundary, physical-property effect, state handling, and product-specific support.

evidence: Reviewed observed rows/bytes/partition distributions, optimizer and transition time, reused/discarded work, task counts, locality, CPU, network, spill, memory, tails, retries, and fleet cost.
Confirmed no universal partition target, skew factor/floor, broadcast cap, memory percentage, margin, cooldown, revision count, or optimizer budget is prescribed.
Confirmed production claims require enabled/disabled differential runs, shadow decisions, matched cohorts, rule/workload/connector canaries, kill switches, and rollback.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Applied-rule count, estimate correction, and final-plan cost are not mislabeled as realized query or fleet benefit.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed control-loop phases, physical plan versioning, observation contracts, decision boundaries, remaining-cost economics, error sensitivity, parallelism, skew, join revision, properties, state, retries, convergence, controls, telemetry, testing, and rollout.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable plan epochs, selected-attempt statistics, immutable revision events, stable-materialization identifiers, candidate legality/feasibility filters, atomic fencing, bounded optimizer/control state, hysteresis, fallback, causal metrics, shadowing, canarying, kill switches, and recovery. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from feedback-loop fundamentals through safe boundaries, physical transformations, distributed state/recovery, stability, and evaluation. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover cost gates, coalescing, partial evidence, broadcast memory, skew, shuffle compatibility, fencing, hysteresis, recovery, executable calculations, control records, parallelism, join revision, outer-join skew, and rollout.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark/Flink/Trino maintainer, Adaptive Query Processing/mid-query reoptimization/Spark SQL author, optimizer/database/distributed-systems/control-theory/scheduler/storage/platform/SRE/performance/security specialist, connector operator, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
